title: Formal runner admission path equivalence and failure totality
hypothesis: A single repository-path admission module can make relative, dot-segment and absolute representations of the same trusted evidence/output locations observationally equivalent, reject every escape or stale-evidence case before formal work, and still write a self-hashed failure receipt for every rejected invocation.

observedFailures.lesson: A nested writable mountpoint absent from the frozen image prevented every container launch; the analyzer was also not total over null observations.
A producer-only preflight did not exercise the analyzer's actual schema-consumer boundary.
An accepted full-shaped preflight did not exercise the formal runner's exact relative CLI path shape; admission failed before its try/finally boundary.

requirements: Commit and push this exact spec and protocol before creating any B53-E1 tool byte or output root.
Commit and push all three exact tool bytes before creating the formal root.
The formal run is single-use. Retain any failure; repair requires a new experiment ID.

evidenceInput.resolution: Resolve CLI spelling against the declared repository root, then require the resolved path and realpath to be identical and strictly below the repository realpath.
git: latest path-affecting commit is an ancestor of the exact configured origin branch
preflight record is canonical-self-hashed and status ACCEPTED
all declared tool hashes equal the current tool bytes

formalOutput.resolution: Resolve CLI spelling against the declared repository root and require its nearest existing ancestor realpath to remain strictly below the repository realpath.
formalOutput.freshness: target must not exist as a file, directory or symbolic link
formalOutput.materialization: admission returns the canonical absolute target but does not create it

attemptLedger.root: a separately declared fresh repository-contained root created before semantic admission
attemptLedger.success: write one canonical self-hashed admission.json and receipt.json
attemptLedger.failure: write one canonical self-hashed failure.json and receipt.json even when evidence/output admission rejects
attemptLedger.verdict: scientificVerdict is always null; this experiment tests execution infrastructure only

canonicalIdentity.representation: repository-relative POSIX path plus file SHA/self-hash/tool bindings
forbiddenInputs: current working directory outside the declared repository

operationContract.gitChildProcesses: observed and reported exactly; no fixed count claim before implementation

decision.supportedWhen: All fourteen gates pass, all 17 cases match their frozen outcome/reason, every case has a valid receipt, and 32 or more independent semantic attacks are rejected.
decision.invalidated: Any tool/process failure produces scientificVerdict null and forbids same-ID repair or rerun.

nonClaims: This does not repair or rerun B52-D12.14-H2.
This does not prove Blender, Docker, remote Git hosting or arbitrary filesystem behavior.
A local bare origin emulates pushed-commit ancestry only; it is not remote attestation.
Path admission totality does not prove downstream analyzer, renderer or scientific correctness.
No production compiler behavior changes unless a later integration experiment preregisters adoption.
promotionBoundary: If supported, future one-shot experiment runners may preregister adoption of the B53-E1 admission module. Existing frozen runners and evidence remain immutable. The next integration must still revalidate B01/B02 structure hashes if it changes compiler orchestration.
